arxiv-1806-04699.title: Capsule Routing for Sound Event Detection
arxiv-1806-04699.creator: Turab Iqbal, Yong Xu, Qiuqiang Kong and Wenwu Wang
arxiv-1806-04699.description: Abstract The detection of acoustic scenes is a challenging problem in which environmental sound events must be detected from a given audio signal. This includes classifying the events as well as estimating their onset and offset times. We approach this problem with a neural network architecture that uses the recently-proposed capsule routing mechanism.

arxiv-1909-05885.title: Analyzing machine-learned representations: A natural language case study
arxiv-1909-05885.description: Abstract As modern deep networks become more complex, and get closer to human-like capabilities in certain domains, the question arises of how the representations and decision rules they learn compare to the ones in humans. In this work, we study representations of sentences in one such artificial system for natural language processing.

arxiv-2208-07927.title: Semi-supervised Transfer Learning for Evaluation of Model Classification Performance
arxiv-2208-07927.creator: Linshanshan Wang, Xuan Wang, Katherine P. Liao, Tianxi Cai
arxiv-2208-07927.description: Abstract In many modern machine learning applications, frequent encounters of covariate shift and label scarcity have posed challenges to robust model training and evaluation. Numerous transfer learning methods have been developed to robustly adapt the model itself to some unlabeled target populations using existing labeled data in a source population.

arxiv-2212-09357.title: Nonlinear acoustic characterization of heterogeneous plasticity in bent aluminium samples
arxiv-2212-09357.creator: Carolina Espinoza, Vicente Salinas, Makarena Osorio, Edgar Pío, Claudio Aguilar, Fernando Lund, Nicolás Mujica
arxiv-2212-09357.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Carolina Espinoza, Vicente Salinas, Makarena Osorio, Edgar Pío, Claudio Aguilar, Fernando Lund, Nicolás Mujica. Knowledge of the state of plastic deformation in metallic structures is vital to prevent failure. This is why non-destructive acoustic tests based on the measurement of first order elastic constants have been developed and intensively used. However, plastic deformations, which are usually heterogeneous in space, may be invisible to these methods if the variation of the elastic constants is too small.

arxiv-2302-10612.title: Tree-Based Machine Learning Methods For Vehicle Insurance Claims Size Prediction
arxiv-2302-10612.creator: Edossa Merga Terefe 1,2
arxiv-2302-10612.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Edossa Merga Terefe 1,2. Abstract

Vehicle insurance claims size prediction needs methods to efficiently handle these claims. Machine learning (ML) is one of the methods that solve this problem. Tree-based ensemble learning algorithms are highly effective and widely used ML methods. This study considers how vehicle insurance providers incorporate ML methods in their companies and explores how the models can be applied to insurance big data.

arxiv-2306-17594.title: On numerical realizations of Shannon’s sampling theorem
arxiv-2306-17594.creator: Melanie Kircheis, Daniel Potts, Manfred Tasche
arxiv-2306-17594.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Melanie Kircheis, Daniel Potts, Manfred Tasche. In this paper, we discuss some numerical realizations of Shannon’s sampling theorem. First we show the poor convergence of classical Shannon sampling sums by presenting sharp upper and lower bounds of the norm of the Shannon sampling operator. In addition, it is known that in the presence of noise in the samples of a bandlimited function, the convergence of Shannon sampling series may even break down completely.

arxiv-2307-00906.title: A data-driven kinetic model for opinion dynamics with social network contacts
arxiv-2307-00906.creator: G. Albi, E. Calzola, G. Dimarco
arxiv-2307-00906.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by G. Albi, E. Calzola, G. Dimarco. Opinion dynamics is an important and very active area of research that delves into the complex processes through which individuals form and modify their opinions within a social context. The ability to comprehend and unravel the mechanisms that drive opinion formation is of great significance for predicting a wide range of social phenomena such as political polarization, the diffusion of misinformation, the formation of public consensus, and the emergence of collective behaviors.

arxiv-2308-03849.title: One-loop Effective Action up to Dimension Eight: Integrating out Heavy Fermion(s) Preprint:
arxiv-2308-03849.creator: Joydeep Chakrabortty, Shakeel Ur Rahaman, Kaanapuli Ramkumar
arxiv-2308-03849.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Joydeep Chakrabortty, Shakeel Ur Rahaman, Kaanapuli Ramkumar. We present the universal one-loop effective action up to dimension eight after integrating out heavy fermion(s) using the Heat-Kernel method. We have discussed how the Dirac operator being a weak elliptic operator, the fermionic operator still can be written in the form of a strong elliptic one such that the Heat-Kernel coefficients can be used to compute the fermionic effective action. This action captures the footprint of both the CP conserving as well as violating UV interactions.

arxiv-2401-03696.title: Stability of rarefaction waves under periodic perturbation for a rate-type viscoelastic system
arxiv-2401-03696.creator: Lin Chang, Duo Liu, Weiqiang Zhang
arxiv-2401-03696.description: Abstract . In this paper, a rarefaction wave under space-periodic perturbation for the 3 × 3 3\times 3 rate-type viscoelastic system is considered. It is shown that if the initial perturbation around the rarefaction wave is suitably small, then the solution of the rate-type viscoelastic system tends to the rarefaction wave.

arxiv-2401-07735.title: Plücker Coordinates and the Rosenfeld Planes
arxiv-2401-07735.creator: Jian Qiu
arxiv-2401-07735.description: Abstract The exceptional compact hermitian symmetric space EIII is the quotient E 6 / S p i n ( 10 ) × ℤ 4 U ( 1 ) E_{6}/Spin(10)\times_{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}U(1) . We introduce the Plücker coordinates which give an embedding of EIII into ℂ ​ P 26 \mathbb{C}P^{26} as a projective subvariety. The subvariety is cut out by 27 Plücker relations.

arxiv-2407-05559.title: Testing the cosmic distance duality relation using Type Ia supernovae and radio quasars through model-independent methods
arxiv-2407-05559.creator: Fan Yang, Xiangyun Fu, Bing Xu, Kaituo Zhang, Yang Huang, Ying Yang
arxiv-2407-05559.description: Abstract In this work, we perform a cosmological-model-independent test on the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) by comparing the angular diameter distance (ADD) obtained from the compact radio quasars (QSOs) with the luminosity distance (LD) from the Pantheon Type Ia supernovae (SNIa) sample.

arxiv-2502-06998.title: Resonances of compressible stars in precessing orbits around a spinning black hole
arxiv-2502-06998.creator: Matteo Stockinger, Masaru Shibata
arxiv-2502-06998.description: Abstract In our previous paper, we reported the presence of a new resonance of an incompressible star orbiting a spinning black hole and showed that it can set in before the tidal disruption limit if the star has an inclined spherical orbit around the black hole.

arxiv-2503-16947.title: Henning Samtleben
arxiv-2503-16947.creator: ENS de Lyon, CNRS, LPENSL, UMR5672, 69342, Lyon cedex 07, France
arxiv-2503-16947.description: Abstract We review exceptional field theories as the duality-covariant reformulation of maximal supergravity theories in ten and eleven dimensions, that make the underlying exceptional symmetries explicit. Beyond their structural role in unifying the various maximal supergravities, we illustrate how they also provide access to very efficient techniques for tackling concrete computational problems in supergravity.

arxiv-2508-21164.title: Quantifying Label-Induced Bias in Large Language Model Self- and Cross-Evaluations
arxiv-2508-21164.creator: Muskan Saraf, Sajjad Rezvani Boroujeni, Justin Beaudry, Hossein Abedi, Tom Bush
arxiv-2508-21164.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate outputs, yet their judgments may be influenced. This study examines bias in self- and cross-model evaluations by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude under four conditions: no labels, true labels, and two false-label scenarios.

arxiv-2509-03576.title: How similar are narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies and high-z type 1 AGN?
arxiv-2509-03576.creator: M. Berton 1, E. Järvelä 2, A. Tortosa 3, C. Mazzucchelli 4
arxiv-2509-03576.description: Abstract The recent observations of highly accreting supermassive black holes (SMBH) at very high redshift ( > > 4) with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) allowed us to shed light for the very first time on the early evolutionary phases of active galactic nuclei (AGN).

arxiv-2510-26760.title: Detection of non-Gaussian quantum correlations through measurement-after-interaction protocols
arxiv-2510-26760.creator: Jiajie Guo, Feng-Xiao Sun, Matteo Fadel, Qiongyi He
arxiv-2510-26760.description: Abstract Additional state evolutions performed before measurement, also called measurement-after-interactions (MAI) protocols, have shown a great potential for increasing the sensitivity of metrological scenarios. Here, we go beyond this result and show that MAI techniques can significantly enhance the detection capability of witnesses for quantum correlations.

pmc-10553611.title: THU205 A Case Of Infant With Familial-Male Limited Precocious Puberty (FMPP) Inherited From Father Due To An Activating Mutation Of The Luteinizing Hormone/Chorionic Gonadotropin Receptor Gene
pmc-10553611.creator: Han-Wook Yoo, Jihyun Ha, Mo Kyung Jung, Yunha Choi, Eun-Gyong Yoo
pmc-10553611.description: Disclosure: H. Yoo: None. J. Ha: None. M. Jung: None. Y. Choi: None. E. Yoo: None.We present an extremely rare case of FMPP with an activating mutation of the LHCGR gene in a Korean infant. A 16-month-old-boy was brought to the out-patient clinic with complaints of pubic hair, acne and rapid growth acceleration.

pmc-10652176.title: Sex‐ and Age Group‐Specific Fracture Incidence Rates Trends for Type 1 and 2 Diabetes Mellitus
pmc-10652176.creator: Mohamad I Nasser, Annika Vestergaard Kvist, Peter Vestergaard, Richard Eastell, Andrea M Burden, Morten Frost
pmc-10652176.description: The incidence of major osteoporotic fractures has declined in men and women in Western countries over the last two decades. Although fracture risk is higher in persons with diabetes mellitus, trends of fractures remain unknown in men and women with diabetes.

pmc-11330048.title: The relationship between body mass index and cerebrospinal fluid pressure in children with pseudotumor cerebri
pmc-11330048.creator: Yakup Çağ, Safiye Güneş Sağer, Merve Akçay, İsmail Kaytan, Elif Söbü, Aydan Erdem, Yasemin Akın
pmc-11330048.description: BackgroundChildhood obesity has become a major global health problem. Obesity is associated with major health problems, such as diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular disease. Obesity is also considered a risk factor for Pseudotumor cerebri (PTC). The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between body mass index (BMI), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) pressure in patients with pseudotumor cerebri.

pmc-11459448.title: Cadmium and silver complexes of a pyridine containing ligand: syntheses, structural studies, biological activity and docking studies†
pmc-11459448.creator: Azza A. Hassoon, Stacey J. Smith, Roger G. Harrison
pmc-11459448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The current study aimed to synthesize seven new metal coordination complexes (Q1–Q7) with potential biomedical applications. Novel mononuclear, polynuclear and mixed-ligand coordination compounds of the elements, cadmium(ii) and silver(i) derived from a pyridine containing ligand (2,4,6-tris-(2-pyridyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TPT)) have been synthesized successfully with the general formulae [Cd(TPT)Cl6]·H2O and [Agx(TPT)y(L)2(ClO4)](ClO4)z (x = 1,2,3, y = 1,2,3, L = PPh3 or phen, z = 1,2).

pmc-11548005.title: The Administration of Resveratrol and Vitamin C Reduces Oxidative Stress in Postmenopausal Women—A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-11548005.creator: Araceli Montoya-Estrada, Aline Yunuen García-Cortés, José Romo-Yañez, Guillermo F Ortiz-Luna, Arturo Arellano-Eguiluz, Aurora Belmont-Gómez, Vivian Lopéz-Ugalde, Guadalupe León-Reyes, Arturo Flores-Pliego, Aurora Espejel-Nuñez, Juan Mario Solis-Paredes, Enrique Reyes-Muñoz, Akiko Kojima-Yuasa, Carol
pmc-11548005.description: In postmenopausal women, due to endocrine changes, there is an increase in oxidative stress (OS) that predisposes them to cardiovascular and metabolic alterations. Sixty-one percent of women in this stage require a primary therapeutic strategy to decrease OS. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of resveratrol and vitamin C on OS in postmenopausal women.

pmc-12358621.title: First night effect alters occipital brain connectivity in horses
pmc-12358621.creator: Jürgen Bergeler, Astrid Liske-Schmitz, Thomas Schmitz, Nora Vanessa de Camp
pmc-12358621.description: The First Night Effect is a phenomenon whereby sleep duration and quality are compromised in unfamiliar environments or situations. Horses are often transported to new locations, such as sporting events. We wanted to know if the First Night Effect is also detectable in horses in two different populations.

pmc-12589117.title: Genetic and epigenetic alterations at secondary resistance after continued decitabine-based treatment of acute myeloid leukemia in the randomized phase II DECIDER trial

However, initially responsive disease eventually develops secondary resistance [1–4]. Resistance against DEC may result from alterations in pyrimidine metabolism, e.g.

pmc-12661688.title: Validation of an AI-Based platform for structured diagnosis of headache disorders using ICHD-3 criteria
pmc-12661688.creator: João Brainer Clares de Andrade, Thiago Bulhões da Silva Costa, Júlia Lima Vasconcelos, Thiago Luís Marques Lopes, Mateus Dutra Balsells, Vinícius Luiz Cristofolini, Sophia Oliveira Querobin, Flavio Moura Rezende Filho
pmc-12661688.description: BackgroundThe diagnosis of headache disorders remains a clinical challenge, particularly for non-specialists, due to the complexity of the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3), and the absence of biomarkers. Large language models (LLMs) represent a promising tool to support accurate and scalable diagnostic classification, especially in resource-limited settings.

pmc-13475242.title: Homologous Tremella fuciformis semi-IPN hydrogels with entanglement-assisted network stabilization for near-neutral pH-responsive photodamage therapy
pmc-13475242.creator: Fei Lin, Huimin Xie, Fang Luo, Zhenyu Lin, Yong Wang, Bin Qiu, Yanjing Huang
pmc-13475242.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Healthy skin maintains a weakly acidic surface pH (4.1-5.8), whereas barrier disruption and acute inflammation may shift the local microenvironment toward near-neutral conditions. However, most stimuli-responsive hydrogels are designed for acidic environments, limiting their suitability for photodamaged skin. To address this, we developed a homologous semi-interpenetrating polymer network (semi-IPN) hydrogel by integrating native Tremella fuciformis polysaccharides (TFPs), oxidized TFPs (OTFPs), and carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS) for near-neutral pH-responsive transdermal delivery of quercetin (QT).

pmc-13543323.title: Trophies for All? Children's and Adolescents’ Reasoning About Inclusive Versus Selective Awards
pmc-13543323.creator: Shuai Shao, Gail D. Heyman
pmc-13543323.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). How do children and adolescents reason about the consequences of institutional reward systems? We examined developmental differences in reasoning about inclusive versus selective awards in a youth sports context. Participants in two age groups (43 in the 7‐ to 9‐year‐old age group and 44 in the 15‐ to 18‐year‐old age group; 46% female, 49% male, 5% other or preferred not to say; majority Asian/White; USA, 2024–2025) read scenarios in which trophies were awarded either to all participants or only to top performers

pmc-13614498.title: A Qualitative Study of Strength, Hope, and Meaning: Multi-Stakeholder Perspectives on Spiritual Care for Breast Cancer
pmc-13614498.creator: Hansen Maikel Su, Suhartini Ismail, Awal Prasetyo
pmc-13614498.description: Objective:To explore the multi-stakeholder experiences of spiritual care for breast cancer patients from the perspectives of patients, families, medical personnel, and religious leaders.Methods:This qualitative descriptive study employed Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis. A purposive sample of 20 participants (five patients, five family members, five medical personnel, and five religious leaders) was recruited in Semarang, Indonesia.

pmc-13680907.title: RESONANCE: Protocol for a Nationwide Cohort Study of Chronic Liver Diseases Using the French National Health Data System
pmc-13680907.creator: Aurore Baron, Laure Tron, Frédéric Balusson, Vaele Zannou, Victoria Mignot, Anne Ego, Anna Borowick, Thomas Decaens, Emmanuel Oger, Sébastien Bailly, Charlotte Costentin
pmc-13680907.description: BackgroundChronic liver diseases (CLDs) are frequent in Europe, including in France, and are mainly driven by alcohol, metabolic dysfunction (diabetes and obesity), and viral hepatitis. Although risk factors are well established and easy to identify, CLDs are frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage, translating into poor prognosis.
